claim: Far transfer from training in one cognitive domain (chess, music, working memory, video games) to general cognition is near zero once active controls and publication bias are handled; near transfer is real. Independent large-N support exists (Owen 2010, N=11,430), but the synthesis is still dominated by one research group.
agent_test: Train the scaffold on tasks of type A; test on unrelated type B at equal tokens with an active-control scaffold (same length, no content).
audit_note: Owen 2010 (N=11,430, no transfer) confirmed independently; most other sources are Sala and Gobet papers, as the claim itself admits; 'near zero' holds for music with active/random designs (g about -0.02 to 0.06) and WM 0.05.

claim: Effect sizes in training-transfer studies shrink as control quality rises (passive to active control): music 0.25 to 0.03; WM 0.18 to 0.05; chess modest effects with almost no active controls.
agent_test: Compare scaffold vs a length-matched placebo scaffold, not vs bare prompt.
audit_note: Numbers match (music 0.25 to 0.03, WM 0.18 to 0.05, chess one active-control study at 0.10) but they come from one Sala and Gobet paper; the other listed sources are the same authors' follow-up or a coauthor's editorial, so there is no independent confirmation.

claim: A large randomised trial of chess lessons (about 1,900 per arm, 25-30 h) found no effect on any outcome, against a meta-analytic 0.34-0.38 d from weaker designs.
agent_test: Treat small gains from uncontrolled scaffold ablations as suspect; require a randomised, item-matched control.

claim: Action video game effects are larger in cross-sectional (g=0.55) than intervention studies (g=0.34); critics find demand characteristics, near-zero latent relations, and null training meta-analysis.
agent_test: Fix prompts and seeds before assigning conditions; blind graders to arm.

claim: Deliberate practice explains much variance in games (26%), music (21%), sports (18%), little in education (4%) and professions (<1%); it is necessary but not sufficient.
agent_test: Not directly testable; informs that more iterations (practice) alone do not guarantee skill: compare more rounds of O-operators vs better-chosen ones at equal tokens.
audit_note: Numbers match the Macnamara et al abstract (2014, later erratum); 'necessary but not sufficient' is an interpretation consistent with the authors' conclusion; Hambrick 2020 is a coauthor follow-up, not independent.

claim: Expert chess skill rests on large stores of chunks and templates; in Gobet and Simon (1998, N = 26) masters recalled about 92% of game positions but only about 19% of random ones (experts 13.8%, class A 12.4%, skill effect on random positions not significant), so the advantage largely shrinks, though not entirely, for structure that does not match learned patterns.
agent_test: Give the agent a retrievable store of solved-pattern chunks; test on structured vs scrambled problems at equal tokens.
audit_note: The 92%/19% recall figures could not be checked (Brunel PDF returned 503; PubMed abstract has no numbers), and 'the advantage vanishes' conflicts with the Sala and Gobet 2017 meta-analysis (r = .41, experts better in 49 of 55 samples) showing a reduced but real expert advantage on random material; in the single study the skill effect on random recall was just non-significant (N = 26).
claim_before_audit: Expert skill in chess rests on large stores of domain-specific chunks/templates; masters recall about 92% of game positions but about 19% of random ones, so the advantage vanishes for structure that does not match learned patterns.

claim: Expert eye movements show fast detection of relevant regions, not more looking; the advantage is in the first fixations, and it is domain-bound.
agent_test: Add an early relevance-filter pass; check it saves tokens while keeping accuracy in-domain.
audit_note: Sheridan and Reingold 2014 (experts distinguish relevant from irrelevant regions earlier, 'early part of the trial') is supported, but the only other source is the same authors' 2017 review of that and related work, so one lab; 'first fixations' is a loose paraphrase of 'early part of the trial'.

claim: Expert-style visual span and holistic processing do not carry to control tasks or neighbouring domains.
agent_test: Evaluate any expert-persona or expert-template feature on a held-out domain.

claim: Persona prompts ('you are an expert X') give no reliable accuracy gain on factual multiple-choice: 162 roles, 2,410 MMLU items, in-domain match coefficient 0.004; automatic persona selection is no better than random. With larger closed models (GPT-4) persona prompts averaged slightly higher (91.06 to 92.28 arithmetic) but flipped right answers to wrong on some items; effect is task dependent.
agent_test: Replicate with our agent: persona vs none on the same items at equal tokens.

claim: Persona benefit appears only in open-ended tasks judged by a model (48.5% vs 23% preference), so conclusions depend on task and judge.
agent_test: Test persona on both a verifiable benchmark and an LLM-judged one; report both.

claim: Models trained or prompted in a narrow condition fail on a rule twist: GPT-4 chess opening legality 100% default vs 21% counterfactual (below the 50% chance of the balanced task), 61% with CoT; GPT-3.5 73% vs 4%.
schema_part: G (verify rule use), O (test counterfactual twin)
agent_test: Run counterfactual twins of our test items; log the gap with and without the scaffold.

claim: For math-tuned LLMs, transfer depends on the training method: on Qwen3-14B with the same math data, RL raised non-reasoning average 45.7 to 53.2 while SFT dropped it to 29.0 (TI -104.1); most of 20+ open models failed to transfer.
schema_part: none (design warning: scaffold gains may not transfer)
agent_test: Measure scaffold gain on in-domain vs out-of-domain benchmarks separately.
audit_note: Numbers match Huan et al (base 45.7, RL 53.2, SFT no-think 29.0, TI -104.1); the 'SFT' figure is the no-think variant.

claim: Game-based RL transfers to reasoning benchmarks in models: SPIRAL +10.5 points (34.0 to 44.5, Qwen3-4B); ViGaL Snake+Rotation math avg 47.7 to 50.6; but SPIRAL's own SFT game baseline also rose (39.7), so the gain is not purely game-specific.
agent_test: Not testable without training; supports a non-training reading only as caution.

claim: Contrary to human far-transfer nulls, training on code improves non-code abilities in LLMs (up to +8.2% relative NL reasoning), while narrow finetuning on insecure code produces broad misalignment (19.8% on GPT-4o vs about 0% controls).
agent_test: Check that a domain-specific scaffold module does not shift behaviour on unrelated prompts.
audit_note: 19.8% is on the selected free-form questions (about 6% on the preregistered set); +8.2% is the best-variant relative NL reasoning gain when code is added in pre-training, a different regime from narrow finetuning.

claim: Expert-level skill can arise from data in one narrow domain without search (270M transformer, Lichess blitz 2895 vs humans, 2299 vs bots) and models encode board state and skill level internally; none of these papers tests transfer out of chess.
agent_test: None directly; shows narrow skill needs no general scaffold.
audit_note: Training labels come from Stockfish search (supervised distillation), so 'without search' means at test time only; the Elo 2895 vs humans and 2299 vs bots, 270M size match.

claim: Machine-derived concepts can teach top human experts in a narrow domain, with gains of 6 to 42 percentage points among 4 grandmasters; improvement was uneven and not tested out of domain.
agent_test: Not testable on our agent.

claim: Eye-tracking-derived human attention used as a training signal improves code models in every tested cell (36/36 positive, up to +13.17% BLEU-4).
agent_test: Cannot test without finetuning; note as a way expert strategy is injected.

claim: Teaching experience is a poor predictor of teacher effectiveness and perceptual expertise can interfere with other perception (cars vs faces); experience does not guarantee generalising skill.
agent_test: Do not use accumulated context length as a proxy for competence.

claim: In SPIRAL, SFT on the same game trajectories gives a large share of the reasoning gain (Qwen3-4B 34.0 to 39.7 vs RL 44.5; Qwen3-8B 39.5 to 46.1 vs 49.6), so game-to-reasoning transfer is partly data and style exposure; no non-game synthetic control was run.
agent_test: Compare game-trained model against a model trained on non-game synthetic tasks with matched format and token count.

claim: Forgetting after fine-tuning is predicted by forward KL shift from the base policy (R2 0.96 toy, 0.71 LLM); on-policy RL stays near the base, SFT can drift far. Prompt scaffolds change no weights.
schema_part: none (design rationale for scaffolding over SFT)
agent_test: Check a scaffolded agent on held-out tasks outside the scaffold domain to confirm no loss against bare prompt.
audit_note: R2 0.96 (toy) and 0.71 (LLM) are in Shenfeld et al; Chu et al does not measure KL shift so only one source supports the numbers; 'prompt scaffolds change no weights' is a logical statement, not a sourced one.

claim: Narrow in-context examples can cause broad misaligned behaviour on unrelated queries (EM 1 to 24% with 16 examples, as few as 2 examples; larger models more susceptible), so prompt-level domain modules can contaminate other domains.
agent_test: Run unrelated benign queries after loading each domain module; flag changed style or advice quality.

claim: Intrinsic self-verification without new information does not improve reasoning and often lowers it (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0 over rounds); it helps only with oracle signals.
agent_test: Compare rule-restating or tool-backed verification against plain re-asking at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Meaningless filler tokens can replace chain of thought in small transformers trained for it (3SUM-type task: CoT 95.1, filler 93.6, none 78.7), so part of a scaffold's gain can be extra computation, not content.
agent_test: Always include a length-matched placebo scaffold.

claim: Action-game training effects did not replicate in supervised experiments with active controls: practice gains were equal for action, cognitive and no-game groups (RT speed-up 51 vs 59 ms; Bayes factors favoured the null).
agent_test: Use active controls and full-range analysis, not extreme groups.
